name: Geographical Discoveries
description: Questions covering: Great Sailors, Continent Exploration, Famous Passages and Straits...

questions.question: Which Portuguese sailor became the first European to round the southern tip of Africa in 1488?
questions.explanation_correct: Bartolomeu Dias named the southern cape the Cape of Storms, which King John II later renamed the Cape of Good Hope.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Vasco da Gama reached India, Magellan led the circumnavigation of the Earth, and Henry the Navigator was a patron of explorers but rarely sailed himself.

questions.question: Which explorer in Spanish service reached the Americas in 1492, believing he had found a route to India?
questions.explanation_correct: Christopher Columbus landed on the island of San Salvador in the Bahamas on October 12, 1492, launching the Age of Discovery.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Amerigo Vespucci proved it was a new continent, Balboa discovered the Pacific Ocean, and Cortés conquered the Aztec Empire.

questions.question: Which Portuguese explorer in 1498 was the first to reach India by sea from Europe around Africa?
questions.explanation_correct: Vasco da Gama's expedition landed in Calicut, India, opening a direct trade route for spices.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dias only reached South Africa, Cabral discovered Brazil, and Almeida was the first viceroy of India.

questions.question: Who led the first expedition to attempt a circumnavigation of the Earth starting in 1519, before dying in the Philippines?
questions.explanation_correct: Magellan organized and led the Spanish expedition, discovering the strait that bears his name, before he was killed in the Philippines.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Elcano completed the voyage, Drake circumnavigated decades later, and Cook lived in the 18th century.

questions.question: Which Spanish captain actually brought the only surviving ship of Magellan's expedition back to Spain in 1522?
questions.explanation_correct: Elcano commanded the ship 'Victoria' during the difficult return across the Indian Ocean and around Africa.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Magellan was already dead, Albo was the pilot, and Pigafetta was the chronicler of the expedition.

questions.question: After which Italian traveler and cartographer was the New World named 'America'?
questions.explanation_correct: Vespucci was the first to describe the newly discovered lands as 'Mundus Novus' (New World) in his letters.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Columbus believed these lands were part of Asia, Verrazzano explored the North American coast, and Cabot sailed for England.

questions.question: Which Portuguese sailor discovered the coast of Brazil in 1500 while originally sailing to India?
questions.explanation_correct: Cabral made a wide arc in the Atlantic (volta do mar) to avoid unfavorable winds and accidentally reached South America.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Gama discovered the route to India earlier, Albuquerque conquered Malacca, and Corte-Real explored Newfoundland.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador became the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from the Isthmus of Panama in 1513?
questions.explanation_correct: Balboa named the newly discovered waters the 'South Sea' and claimed them for the Spanish crown.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pizarro conquered Peru, de Soto explored the Mississippi River, and Ponce de León discovered Florida.

questions.question: Which Italian sailor in English service reached the coast of North America (Newfoundland) in 1497?
questions.explanation_correct: John Cabot (Giovanni Caboto) gave England its first territorial claims in North America.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Vespucci explored the south of the continent, Columbus the Caribbean islands, and Sebastian Cabot was John's son who traveled later.

questions.question: Which French explorer in 1534 explored the Gulf of St. Lawrence and claimed these lands for France under the name Canada?
questions.explanation_correct: Cartier made three voyages to North America and produced the first maps of the St. Lawrence River.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Champlain founded Quebec, La Salle claimed Louisiana for France, and Nicolet explored Lake Michigan.

questions.question: Which English privateer and sailor became the second person in history to circumnavigate the Earth in 1577–1580 on the Golden Hind?
questions.explanation_correct: Drake plundered Spanish colonies in the Pacific and returned rich, for which Queen Elizabeth I knighted him.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Raleigh established colonies in Virginia, Hawkins was a trader, and Frobisher sought the Northwest Passage.

questions.question: Which Flemish cartographer created a cylindrical world map in 1569 that was extremely useful for marine navigation?
questions.explanation_correct: Mercator's projection preserved angles, allowing sailors to plot a course as a straight line (loxodrome).
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ortelius published the first modern world atlas, Blaeu was a map publisher, and Hondius continued Mercator's work.

questions.question: Which Dutch traveler discovered Australia in 1606, landing on the Cape York Peninsula?
questions.explanation_correct: Janszoon on the ship 'Duyfken' mapped about 300 km of the coast, initially thinking it was part of New Guinea.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Tasman discovered Tasmania and New Zealand, Hartog the west coast of Australia, and Roggeveen Easter Island.

questions.question: Which Dutch sailor discovered the island now known as Tasmania and New Zealand in 1642?
questions.explanation_correct: Tasman named the island Van Diemen's Land after the colony's governor, and New Zealand was believed to be part of a southern continent.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Barents died on Novaya Zemlya, Janszoon explored northern Australia, and Heemskerck was an admiral.

questions.question: Which English explorer in the 18th century made three great voyages to the Pacific, mapping New Zealand and eastern Australia?
questions.explanation_correct: James Cook commanded the 'Endeavour' and ultimately disproved the myth of a giant, fertile continent Terra Australis Incognita.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dampier described Australia earlier, Anson circumnavigated the globe as a naval admiral, and Flinders was the first to circumnavigate Australia.

questions.question: Which Norwegian polar explorer became the first person to reach the South Pole on December 14, 1911?
questions.explanation_correct: Amundsen beat the British expedition of Robert Scott thanks to superior planning and the use of sled dogs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Scott arrived a month later and died on the return journey, Nansen drifted on the Fram, and Shackleton saved the crew of the Endurance.

questions.question: Which British explorer died in March 1912 on his way back from the South Pole, having lost the race to Amundsen?
questions.explanation_correct: Scott and his four companions died of exhaustion and extreme cold just eleven miles from their main supply depot.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Shackleton did not reach the pole, Mawson explored East Antarctica, and Franklin disappeared in the Arctic in the 19th century.

questions.question: What is the name of the strait separating Asia from North America, explored by Vitus Bering in 1728?
questions.explanation_correct: The Dane Vitus Bering, serving the Russian Empire, proved that Asia and America are not connected by land.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Drake Passage lies south of South America, Cook Strait separates the islands of New Zealand, and the Strait of Magellan lies in Patagonia.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador discovered and explored the Amazon River during his expedition in 1541–1542?
questions.explanation_correct: Orellana sailed the entire length of the river, naming it 'Amazon' after encounters with female warriors of the Tapuya tribe.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pizarro searched for El Dorado on land, Huaman did not explore, and Valdivia was conquering Chile.

questions.question: Which Venetian merchant traveled the Silk Road to China in the 13th century and served at the court of Kublai Khan?
questions.explanation_correct: Marco Polo described his travels in 'The Travels of Marco Polo', which inspired generations of explorers, including Columbus.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Carpine was a papal envoy to the Mongols, Odoric was a missionary, and Conti traveled in the 15th century.

questions.question: Which Norwegian researcher and Nobel laureate drifted on the ship 'Fram' in Arctic ice, attempting to reach the North Pole?
questions.explanation_correct: Nansen proved the existence of Arctic currents and made a spectacular ski dash north with Hjalmar Johansen.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Amundsen won the South Pole, Sverdrup mapped Canadian islands, and Andree died in a balloon expedition.

questions.question: Which Scottish physician and missionary explored the Zambezi River and became the first European to see Victoria Falls?
questions.explanation_correct: Livingstone spent most of his life in Central Africa, searching for the sources of the Nile and fighting the slave trade.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Stanley found Livingstone and explored the Congo River, Park studied the Niger, and Burton discovered Lake Tanganyika.

questions.question: Which journalist and explorer uttered the famous words 'Dr. Livingstone, I presume?' upon finding the missionary in 1871?
questions.explanation_correct: Stanley organized a rescue expedition funded by the 'New York Herald' and later became a prominent explorer of the Congo.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Speke discovered Lake Victoria, Baker explored Nile tributaries, and Cameron was the first to cross Africa from east to west.

questions.question: Which English traveler was the first European to reach Lake Victoria and identify it as the source of the Nile in 1858?
questions.explanation_correct: Speke traveled with Burton, but reached the northern shore of the lake alone and named it after the Queen.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Burton contested Speke's theory, preferring Lake Tanganyika, and Baker discovered Lake Albert.

questions.question: Which navigational instrument, measuring the height of celestial bodies above the horizon, replaced the astrolabe in the 18th century?
questions.explanation_correct: The sextant allowed for precise determination of latitude on a moving ship.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The magnetic compass indicates north, the log measures speed, and the compass rose is a design element on maps.

questions.question: Which English clockmaker constructed the first accurate marine chronometer, H4, in 1759, solving the longitude problem?
questions.explanation_correct: Harrison's chronometer kept the time of the home port at sea, allowing the calculation of longitude by comparing local time.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other clockmakers improved chronometer design, but Harrison won the British Parliament's prize.

questions.question: Which strait at the southern tip of South America, bypassed by Cape Horn, was discovered by Magellan's expedition?
questions.explanation_correct: The Strait of Magellan was the key passage between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans before the Panama Canal was built.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Drake Passage lies further south in open ocean, the Beagle Channel separates Tierra del Fuego islands, and Messina is in Italy.

questions.question: Which British explorer led a dramatic expedition on the ship 'Endurance' in 1914–1917, saving all crew members?
questions.explanation_correct: When ice crushed the 'Endurance', Shackleton sailed 800 miles in a lifeboat to South Georgia to bring rescue.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Scott died in 1912, Worsley was the ship's captain, and Mawson explored Antarctica from Australia.

questions.question: What was the legendary passage connecting the Atlantic to the Pacific along Canada's northern coast, first navigated by Amundsen?
questions.explanation_correct: Amundsen sailed through it in 1903–1906 on the small herring boat 'Gjøa'.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The Northeast Passage runs along the coast of Russia, and the Bering Isthmus does not exist.

questions.question: Which Swedish explorer was the first to navigate the Northeast Passage on the ship 'Vega' in 1878–1879?
questions.explanation_correct: Nordenskiold sailed along the coast of Siberia, proving the viability of a trade route north of Eurasia.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Andree flew a balloon to the pole, Hedin explored Central Asia, and Otto Nordenskjold led an Antarctic expedition.

questions.question: Which polar expedition of 1845–1848, aiming to map the Northwest Passage on the ships Erebus and Terror, disappeared without a trace?
questions.explanation_correct: Sir John Franklin and his entire 129-man crew died of cold and hunger after their ships became trapped in ice near King William Island.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Parry and Ross returned successfully, and Nares explored the Arctic much later.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador explored the southwestern regions of today's USA in 1540–1542, discovering the Grand Canyon?
questions.explanation_correct: Coronado searched for the mythical Seven Golden Cities of Cibola, reaching as far as today's Kansas.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Soto explored the southeast of the US, Ponce de Leon Florida, and Cabeza de Vaca survived a shipwreck in Texas.

questions.question: Which Spanish explorer walked across the southern US and northern Mexico after the collapse of the Narvaez expedition in 1528?
questions.explanation_correct: Cabeza de Vaca spent eight years in captivity among Native Americans and as a medicine man before reaching Spanish settlements.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Coronado explored later on horseback, Cortes conquered the Aztecs, and Onate colonized New Mexico.

questions.question: Which French explorer sailed the Mississippi River to its mouth in 1682 and named the region Louisiana after King Louis XIV?
questions.explanation_correct: La Salle claimed the Mississippi basin for France, laying the foundation for the colony of New France.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Champlain explored the Great Lakes, and Marquette and Jolliet were the first to reach the upper Mississippi.

questions.question: Which English sailor in Dutch and English service explored the river in New York and the giant bay in Canada that now bear his name?
questions.explanation_correct: Hudson sought the Northwest Passage, but his crew mutinied in Hudson Bay in 1611 and set him adrift to die.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Baffin and Davis explored straits north of Labrador, and Frobisher searched for gold.

questions.question: What was the name for Spanish and Portuguese navigation charts showing rhumb lines during the Age of Discovery?
questions.explanation_correct: Portolan charts were based on accurate descriptions of ports and compass directions, used mainly for coastal sailing.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mappae mundi were symbolic medieval maps, and T-O maps represented a schematic Christian view of the world.

questions.question: Which Arab traveler in the 14th century covered over 70,000 miles, describing Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia?
questions.explanation_correct: Ibn Battuta recorded his travels in the 'Rihla' (The Journey), exceeding the scope of Marco Polo's travels.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Al-Masudi lived in the 10th century, Ibn Khaldun was a historian, and Al-Idrisi was a cartographer for King Roger II of Sicily.

questions.question: Which Swiss explorer and writer became the first European to reach the ruins of Petra in Jordan and Abu Simbel in Egypt?
questions.explanation_correct: Burckhardt traveled disguised as a Muslim merchant under the name Ibrahim ibn Abdallah.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Barth explored the Sahara, Burton searched for Nile sources, and Niebuhr explored the Arabian Peninsula.

questions.question: Which expedition of 1804–1806, commissioned by President Thomas Jefferson, was the first overland to reach the Pacific through the US?
questions.explanation_correct: Meriwether Lewis and William Clark led the Corps of Discovery from St. Louis to the mouth of the Columbia River on the Pacific.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pike explored the Rocky Mountains, Fremont mapped Oregon, and Astor established fur trading posts.

questions.question: Which American explorer claimed to reach the North Pole in 1909, a claim that was later disputed?
questions.explanation_correct: Peary claimed to reach the pole with Matthew Henson, but analyses of his navigational logs raise serious doubts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cook claimed he reached it in 1908, Byrd flew over it by plane, and Amundsen flew over it by airship.

questions.question: Which traveler from Florence, sailing for the King of France, discovered New York Bay in 1524?
questions.explanation_correct: Verrazzano explored the east coast of North America from North Carolina to Newfoundland.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cabot reached Newfoundland earlier, and Vespucci explored the south of the continent.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador reached Florida in 1513 searching for the legendary Fountain of Youth?
questions.explanation_correct: Ponce de Leon named the land 'La Florida' due to its lush vegetation and landing during the Easter season (Pascua Florida).
questions.explanation_incorrect: Soto explored Florida's interior later, Balboa the Pacific, and Narvaez died in a storm near Texas.

questions.question: Which English explorer studied Lake Tanganyika with Burton, and later died in a mysterious shooting accident before a debate?
questions.explanation_correct: Speke died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound during a hunt, a day before a scheduled debate with Burton on the Nile's source.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Burton survived Speke by many years, Grant was Speke's loyal companion, and Baker explored the Nile independently.

questions.question: Which German naturalist traveled to Latin America in 1799–1804, laying the foundations for modern geography?
questions.explanation_correct: Humboldt described climate zones, the ocean current off Peru (Humboldt Current), and climbed the Chimborazo volcano.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ritter was an academic geographer, Forster traveled with Cook, and Poeppig explored Chile.

questions.question: Which Chinese admiral of the Ming dynasty led seven great naval expeditions to India and Africa in the 15th century?
questions.explanation_correct: Zheng He commanded a huge fleet of 'treasure ships', reaching as far as the coasts of Kenya and Somalia.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Koxinga was a pirate-patriot, Yi Sun-sin a Korean admiral, and Shi Lang conquered Taiwan.

questions.question: Which Danish-born Russian naval officer led the Great Northern Expedition in 1733–1743?
questions.explanation_correct: Bering organized the gigantic effort to map Siberia and Alaska, during which he died on Bering Island.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dezhnev sailed the strait in the 17th century, Wrangel explored northern Siberia, and Kolchak was an explorer and white army admiral.

questions.question: Which Russian Cossack became the first European to sail through the Bering Strait in 1648, beating Bering by 80 years?
questions.explanation_correct: Dezhnev sailed around the easternmost cape of Asia (Cape Dezhnev) in small 'koch' boats.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Yermak conquered Western Siberia, and Poyarkov and Khabarov explored the Amur River.

questions.question: Which Portuguese conquistador conquered Malacca in 1511, securing Portugal's power in the Indian Ocean?
questions.explanation_correct: Albuquerque established the Portuguese spice trade empire by capturing Goa, Malacca, and Ormuz.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Almeida was the first viceroy, Cabral discovered Brazil, and Pereira was a military commander and geographer.

questions.question: Which English explorer in 1553 reached Arkhangelsk and opened a trade route with the Tsardom of Russia?
questions.explanation_correct: Chancellor sought the Northeast Passage. Although his commander Willoughby died, he reached the court of Ivan the Terrible.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Willoughby froze in Lapland, Davis explored Greenland, and Gilbert died in a storm.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador traveled through the southeastern US in 1539–1543, discovering the Mississippi River?
questions.explanation_correct: De Soto died of fever on the banks of the Mississippi, and his body was sunk in the river to hide his death from Native Americans.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Coronado explored the western US, Ponce de Leon Florida, and Valdivia Chile.

questions.question: Which English explorer was the first European to map all of New Zealand and its surrounding waters since Tasman?
questions.explanation_correct: Cook sailed around New Zealand, charting its contours and discovering the strait dividing the islands.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dampier explored western Australia, Byron traveled the Pacific earlier, and Vancouver explored Canada's coast.

questions.question: What is the name of the strait separating Tasmania from mainland Australia, discovered in 1798?
questions.explanation_correct: The strait was named after George Bass, who sailed through it with Matthew Flinders, proving Tasmania is an island.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Torres Strait separates Australia from New Guinea, Dampier is in Indonesia, and Cook is in New Zealand.

questions.question: Which strait separates the northern tip of Australia (Cape York) from the island of New Guinea?
questions.explanation_correct: The strait was discovered by Spanish sailor Luis Vaez de Torres in 1606, sailing with Quiros's expedition.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bass lies south of Australia, Sunda in Indonesia, and Malacca between Sumatra and Malaya.

questions.question: Which ancient scholar of Alexandria wrote the 'Geography' with a coordinate grid, used during the Age of Discovery?
questions.explanation_correct: Ptolemy compiled the geographical knowledge of the Roman Empire, and his rediscovered maps revolutionized Renaissance cartography.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Eratosthenes calculated Earth's circumference, Strabo wrote a descriptive geography, and Pliny an encyclopedia.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador led the conquest and destruction of the Inca Empire starting in 1532?
questions.explanation_correct: Pizarro captured the Inca ruler Atahualpa at Cajamarca and executed him despite receiving a massive ransom.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cortes conquered the Aztecs, Almagro was Pizarro's rival and explored Chile, and Alvarado conquered Guatemala.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador led the conquest of the Aztec Empire in Mexico in 1519–1521?
questions.explanation_correct: Cortes allied with the enemies of the Aztecs and captured the capital Tenochtitlan, imprisoning Moctezuma II.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Pizarro conquered the Incas, Narvaez tried to arrest Cortes, and Balboa discovered the Pacific.

questions.question: Which French explorer founded Quebec City in 1608 and is called the 'Father of New France'?
questions.explanation_correct: Champlain made accurate maps of Canada's coast and the Great Lakes, and allied with the Hurons.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cartier explored earlier, Cabot sailed for England, and Jolliet explored the Mississippi.

questions.question: Which Dutch sailor discovered Easter Island on Easter Sunday in 1722?
questions.explanation_correct: Roggeveen searched for the mythical Terra Australis on behalf of the Dutch West India Company.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Schouten and Le Maire rounded Cape Horn, and Spilbergen was a privateer.

questions.question: Which Dutch sailors discovered Cape Horn in 1616, naming it after a town in the Netherlands?
questions.explanation_correct: Willem Schouten and Jacob Le Maire found a new route to the Pacific, bypassing the Strait of Magellan monopoly.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other duos explored other regions (Australia or the Arctic).

questions.question: Which English nobleman organized the first failed attempts to establish a colony on Roanoke Island in 1585?
questions.explanation_correct: Raleigh funded the expeditions that created the 'Lost Colony' of Roanoke, whose settlers vanished without a trace.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Drake raided coasts, Gilbert explored Newfoundland, and Grenville commanded the colony ships.

questions.question: Which Venetian sailor in Spanish service reached the Rio de la Plata in 1526, naming it to suggest the presence of silver?
questions.explanation_correct: Sebastian Cabot explored the Parana and Paraguay rivers based on legends of the White King and Silver Mountains.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Verrazzano explored the north, Vespucci Brazil's coast, and John Cabot was Sebastian's father.

questions.question: What is the name for a medieval world map showing Asia at the top, Europe on the left, and Africa on the right?
questions.explanation_correct: T-O maps represented a Christian view of the world, where the T divided continents and the O surrounded them with ocean.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Portolans were navigation charts, Mercator used cylindrical projection, and Ptolemy used conic projection.

questions.question: Which American pilot and explorer was the first to fly over the South Pole in 1929?
questions.explanation_correct: Byrd flew over the pole on board the Ford Trimotor airplane named 'Floyd Bennett'.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Peary claimed to reach it on foot, Ellsworth flew across Antarctica later, and Wilkins explored the Arctic.

questions.question: Which Swedish explorer mapped Central Asia in the 19th and 20th centuries, including Tibet and the Taklamakan Desert?
questions.explanation_correct: Hedin located the ruins of Loulan, the sources of the Indus and Brahmaputra, and created valuable maps of Central Asia.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nordenskiold sailed around Siberia, Andree died in a balloon, and Ekholm was a meteorologist.

questions.question: Which Swedish engineer died in 1897 trying to reach the North Pole in the hydrogen balloon 'Ornen'?
questions.explanation_correct: Andree and his two companions crashed on the ice and died on Kvitoya; their remains were only discovered in 1930.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nordenskiold was the first to navigate the Northeast Passage, Hedin explored Central Asia, and Ekholm was a meteorologist who resigned from the balloon mission.

questions.question: Which French admiral and traveler circumnavigated the Earth in 1766–1769, taking the first woman, Jeanne Baret, on board?
questions.explanation_correct: Bougainville described Tahiti, popularizing the myth of an earthly paradise, and the bougainvillea flower was named after him.
questions.explanation_incorrect: La Perouse disappeared in the Pacific, Freycinet explored Australia, and d'Urville discovered Adelie Land.

questions.question: Which French explorer disappeared in the Pacific in 1788 after leaving Botany Bay in Australia?
questions.explanation_correct: La Perouse wrecked his ships 'Boussole' and 'Astrolabe' on reefs around Vanikoro in the Solomon Islands.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bougainville returned successfully, d'Entrecasteaux died searching for La Perouse, and Baudin explored Australia.

questions.question: Which French traveler in the 19th century explored the coasts of Antarctica, naming Adelie Land after his wife?
questions.explanation_correct: D'Urville also brought the famous Greek Venus de Milo sculpture back to France, discovered on Milos.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Charcot explored Antarctica in the 20th century, Bougainville in the 18th century, and Baudin died on Mauritius.

questions.question: Which Spanish traveler in 1606 described the New Hebrides, naming them Austrialia del Espiritu Santo?
questions.explanation_correct: Queiros was a religious mystic searching for the southern continent for Spain and the Church.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Torres was his pilot and sailed west, Mendana discovered the Solomons, and Villalobos named the Philippines.

questions.question: Which Spanish explorer discovered the Solomon Islands in 1567, believing he had found King Solomon's biblical mines?
questions.explanation_correct: Mendana later organized a second tragic expedition, during which he died in the Santa Cruz Islands.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Queiros and Torres participated in later Spanish voyages.

questions.question: Which Spanish traveler in 1542 named islands in the Pacific the 'Philippines' after Prince Philip?
questions.explanation_correct: Villalobos commanded the expedition from Mexico that reached Samar and Leyte, naming them Las Islas Filipinas.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Mendana discovered the Solomons, Elcano circumnavigated the globe, and Legazpi colonized the Philippines.

questions.question: Which British researcher was the first to locate the North Magnetic Pole on the Boothia Peninsula in 1831?
questions.explanation_correct: James Clark Ross did this during the expedition of his uncle John Ross, and later discovered the Ross Sea in Antarctica.
questions.explanation_incorrect: John Ross was his uncle and commander, Parry explored straits, and Franklin went missing.

questions.question: Which Norwegian researcher was the first to cross Greenland on skis from east to west in 1888?
questions.explanation_correct: Nansen and his five-man team cut off their retreat by landing on the uninhabited east coast.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Amundsen won the South Pole, Sverdrup mapped islands in the north, and Johansen accompanied Nansen on the Fram.

questions.question: Which Russian explorer established the first permanent Russian settlement in Alaska at Three Saints Bay in 1784?
questions.explanation_correct: Shelikhov founded the settlement on Kodiak Island and was the driving force behind the Russian-American Company.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Baranov was the first governor of Russian America, Bering discovered the strait, and Kuskov founded Fort Ross.

questions.question: Which Russian governor of Alaska expanded Russian fur posts and founded New Archangel (today's Sitka)?
questions.explanation_correct: Baranov ruled Russian America for nearly 20 years, developing the trade in sea otter furs.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kuskov founded the California post, Shelikhov founded the first colony on Kodiak, and Wrangel was an explorer.

questions.question: Which Russian trader established the southernmost Russian outpost, Fort Ross, in California in 1812?
questions.explanation_correct: Kuskov founded Fort Ross as an agricultural base to supply Alaska with food.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Baranov was his superior, Kotzebue circumnavigated the globe, and Shelikhov died before the fort was built.

questions.question: Which Russian navigator of German descent conducted the first Russian circumnavigation in 1803–1806?
questions.explanation_correct: Krusenstern commanded the 'Nadezhda', aiming to establish relations with Japan and supply Alaska.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Kotzebue commanded later voyages, Bellingshausen discovered Antarctica, and Wrangel explored Siberia.

questions.question: Which Russian admiral led the 1819–1821 expedition that first sighted the ice shelf of Antarctica?
questions.explanation_correct: Bellingshausen on the sloop 'Vostok' circumnavigated Antarctica, discovering Peter I Island and Alexander I Land.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Lazarev captained the second ship 'Mirny', Krusenstern sailed earlier, and Golovnin explored Japan.

questions.question: Which English explorer first entered Frobisher Bay on Baffin Island in 1576, bringing back pyrite mistaken for gold?
questions.explanation_correct: Frobisher made three voyages seeking gold and the Northwest Passage, reaching Frobisher Bay.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Davis and Hudson explored these areas later, and Gilbert drowned off Newfoundland.

questions.question: Which English navigator discovered the strait separating Greenland from Canada in 1585?
questions.explanation_correct: Davis Strait became the main gateway for later searchers of the Northwest Passage.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Frobisher explored south Baffin Island, Baffin mapped the bay, and Hudson the rivers.

questions.question: Which English sailor traveled furthest north in the Canadian Arctic in 1616, mapping a bay named after him?
questions.explanation_correct: Baffin, sailing as pilot with Robert Bylot on the 'Discovery', reached 78° N, a record unbeaten for 230 years.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Davis mapped the strait, Hudson the bay, and Bylot was the expedition captain.

questions.question: Which British explorer studied Antarctica on the 'Erebus' in 1839–1843, discovering Mount Erebus?
questions.explanation_correct: Ross explored the Antarctic coast, named the volcano after his ship, and the shelf ice after himself.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Franklin explored the Arctic, Parry sought the northern passage, and Scott traveled in the 20th century.

questions.question: Which British lieutenant led a 1819–1820 expedition, winning a prize for crossing 110° W longitude in the Arctic?
questions.explanation_correct: Parry wintered on Melville Island on the 'Hecla', proving that polar winter survival was possible.
questions.explanation_incorrect: John Ross was his rival, James Clark Ross studied magnetism, and Franklin died.

questions.question: Which Scottish explorer first entered Lancaster Sound in 1818, mistaken it for a bay blocked by the Croker Mountains?
questions.explanation_correct: Ross turned back, causing a scandal; Parry proved the mountains were a mirage the next year.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other travelers participated without making this error.

questions.question: Which Spanish captain led a colonization expedition from Peru to the Solomons in 1595 after Mendana's death?
questions.explanation_correct: Queiros brought the remnants of the fleet to Manila, and his reports prompted the king to fund another voyage in 1605.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Torres sailed with him later, Legazpi colonized the Philippines earlier, and Fuca sought a Canadian passage.

questions.question: Which Greek sailor in Spanish service claimed to discover a strait in Canada connecting the Pacific and Atlantic in 1592?
questions.explanation_correct: Juan de Fuca (Ioannis Phokas) described the strait separating Vancouver Island from Washington State.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Queiros sought the southern land, Bering the northern strait, and Ulloa the Gulf of California.

questions.question: Which American explorer discovered the Inca city of Machu Picchu in Peru in 1911?
questions.explanation_correct: Bingham led the Yale University expedition and reached the ruins hidden in the Andean cloud forests.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Fawcett disappeared in Brazil looking for City Z, Humboldt traveled a century earlier, and Rondon mapped the Amazon.

questions.question: Which British colonel disappeared in 1925 in Brazil's Mato Grosso while searching for the mythical 'City Z'?
questions.explanation_correct: Fawcett, his son Jack, and Raleigh Rimell vanished without a trace, inspiring numerous search expeditions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other three explorers were famous for their discoveries in Africa.

questions.question: Which French traveler reached Timbuktu in 1828 as the first Christian to return alive across the Sahara?
questions.explanation_correct: Caillie traveled alone disguised as an Arab and received a prize from the Paris Geographical Society.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Laing reached it earlier in 1826 but was murdered, Park explored the Niger, and Barth visited later.

questions.question: Which Scottish surgeon explored the Niger River in 1795–1797, dying during his second expedition in Bussa in 1806?
questions.explanation_correct: Mungo Park wrote a bestselling book on his travels, proving that the Niger River flows east.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Clapperton and Lander explored the lower Niger later, and Laing died in Timbuktu.

questions.question: Which German scholar traveled the Sahara and Sahel in 1850–1855, writing a five-volume work on African anthropology?
questions.explanation_correct: Barth explored the area around Lake Chad and the Niger River, learning local languages and collecting historical manuscripts.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nachtigal explored the central Sahara, Schweinfurth the Congo basin, and Rohlfs Libyan oases.

questions.question: Which Polish explorer and geologist studied Siberia and Lake Baikal, escaping exile after the January Uprising?
questions.explanation_correct: Czekanowski explored the Siberian rivers Lena and Olenyok, and the Czekanowski Mountains were named after him.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Czerski explored mountains around Baikal, Dybowski the lake's fauna, and Pilsudski Ainu culture on Sakhalin.

questions.question: Which Polish geologist described mountain ranges in Eastern Siberia, including the Czerski Mountains named after him?
questions.explanation_correct: Jan Czerski made the first geological surveys of eastern Siberia and died during an expedition at the mouth of the Kolyma River in 1892.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Czekanowski explored the Olenyok, Dybowski was a zoologist, and Tyzenhauz an ornithologist.

questions.question: Which Polish traveler in the 19th century surveyed Australia's highest peak and named it Mount Kosciuszko?
questions.explanation_correct: Strzelecki explored and named the Gippsland region in Victoria and discovered coal and gold deposits in Australia.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other names are not associated with Australian exploration history.

questions.question: Which Polish traveler explored the Limpopo River and Zambezi basin in South Africa in the 19th century?
questions.explanation_correct: Rehman was a geographer and botanist from Lwow University, author of pioneer physical-geographical descriptions of South Africa.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rogozinski, Janikowski, and Tomczek led the Polish expedition to Cameroon.

questions.question: Which Polish explorer led the Polish expedition to Cameroon in 1882–1884 to establish a Polish colony?
questions.explanation_correct: Rogozinski purchased Mondoleh Island, explored Mount Cameroon, and studied Lake Barombi Mbo.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rehman explored South Africa, Strzelecki Australia, and Domeyko was a prominent geologist in Chile.

questions.question: Which Polish geologist spent most of his life in Chile, reorganizing its education and exploring the Atacama Desert?
questions.explanation_correct: Domeyko was rector of the University of Santiago, and the Chilean government named the Cordillera de Domeyko after him.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Rogozinski explored Cameroon, and Czerski and Czekanowski studied Siberia.

questions.question: Which English captain explored the Pacific coast of North America in 1791–1795, including Vancouver Island?
questions.explanation_correct: Vancouver made an extremely detailed survey from California to Alaska, cooperating with Spanish explorers.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cook explored the islands earlier, Bligh was famous for the Bounty mutiny, and Franklin studied the Arctic.

questions.question: Which famous captain of HMS Bounty was set adrift in a launch after a crew mutiny in the Pacific in 1789?
questions.explanation_correct: Bligh sailed over 3,600 nautical miles in an open boat without charts, reaching Timor safely with his loyal crew.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Vancouver and Cook were his commanders in other years, and Byron sailed earlier.

questions.question: Which Spanish captain in 1775 was the first to sail through the Golden Gate into San Francisco Bay?
options: Juan Francisco de la Bodega y Quadra
questions.explanation_correct: Ayala spent several weeks mapping the bay and named Isla de los Alcatraces (Alcatraz).
questions.explanation_incorrect: Heceta discovered the Columbia River mouth, Bodega explored Alaska, and Portola commanded the land expedition.

questions.question: Which Spanish governor led the first land expedition through California in 1769–1770, founding San Diego?
questions.explanation_correct: Portola led the colonization expedition from Mexico, and Father Serra established the first Catholic missions.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ayala explored by sea, Serra was a missionary, and Anza founded San Francisco in 1776.

questions.question: Which strait, only 800 meters wide, connects the Sea of Marmara to the Black Sea, dividing Istanbul?
questions.explanation_correct: The Bosporus is one of the most historically important waterways, now regulated by Turkey under the Montreux Convention.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dardanelles connects Marmara to the Aegean, Gibraltar connects the Atlantic to the Mediterranean, and Bab al-Mandab is in Yemen.

questions.question: Which strait connects the Aegean Sea to the Sea of Marmara, known in antiquity as the Hellespont?
questions.explanation_correct: The Dardanelles was the site of Xerxes' army crossing and the famous Gallipoli campaign in 1915.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Bosporus leads to the Black Sea, Kerch to the Sea of Azov, and Otranto separates Italy from Albania.

questions.question: Which strait separates the island of Sicily from the Italian mainland?
questions.explanation_correct: The Strait of Messina is famous for strong tidal currents, personified in Greek myth as the monsters Scylla and Charybdis.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Otranto lies in eastern Italy, the Strait of Sicily lies between Sicily and Tunisia, and Bonifacio separates Corsica from Sardinia.

questions.question: Which strait separates the island of Corsica from neighboring Sardinia in the Mediterranean?
questions.explanation_correct: The Strait of Bonifacio is known for strong winds, granite rocks, and a narrow passage that is dangerous for shipping.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Messina separates Sicily from Italy, Gibraltar separates Europe from Africa, and Sicily lies to the south.

questions.question: Which strait separates the Malay Peninsula from Sumatra, forming a key route between India and China?
questions.explanation_correct: The Strait of Malacca is one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, historically controlled by the Malacca Sultanate.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Sunda lies between Sumatra and Java, Makassar in Indonesia, and Hormuz in the Persian Gulf.

questions.question: Which strait lies between the Indonesian islands of Sumatra and Java, at the foot of Krakatoa?
questions.explanation_correct: The Sunda Strait connects the Java Sea to the Indian Ocean and witnessed the catastrophic eruption of Krakatoa in 1883.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Malacca lies north of Sumatra, Lombok separates Bali from Lombok, and Makassar separates Borneo from Celebes.

questions.question: Which strait in Indonesia separates Bali and Lombok, forming the Wallace Line zoogeographical boundary?
questions.explanation_correct: The Lombok Strait is very deep, preventing the migration of Asian animals eastward during ice ages.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The other straits lie west of the Wallace Line in the pure Asian zone.

questions.question: Which ancient scholar of Alexandria first calculated the Earth's circumference in the 3rd century BCE?
questions.explanation_correct: Eratosthenes was accurate to within a few percent of the actual value of around 40,075 km.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Ptolemy lived in the 2nd century CE, Aristarchus proposed heliocentrism, and Pythagoras claimed the Earth is a sphere.

questions.question: Which Spanish navigator sailed south of New Guinea in 1606, discovering a strait between it and Australia?
questions.explanation_correct: Torres commanded the 'San Pedro' and charted a dangerous passage through the reefs of Torres Strait.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Queiros abandoned the voyage earlier, while Fuca and Mendana sailed elsewhere.

questions.question: Which English navigator and explorer first mapped a bay in northern Canada for the Muscovy Company in 1616?
questions.explanation_correct: Robert Bylot was captain of the 'Discovery' when pilot Baffin charted Baffin Bay.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Baffin was the pilot, Hudson discovered the southern bay earlier, and Davis explored the strait.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador founded Santiago in 1541, becoming Chile's first governor?
questions.explanation_correct: Valdivia conquered central Chile but was killed in battle by the Mapuche chief Lautaro.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Almagro reached Chile first but returned, and Pizarro and Alvarado operated further north.

questions.question: Which prominent Mapuche chief in Chile defeated and killed Spanish conquistador Pedro de Valdivia in 1553?
questions.explanation_correct: Lautaro had been Valdivia's servant, learning Spanish military tactics and horse riding.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Caupolican was another chief, Galvarino had his hands cut off by Spaniards, and Tupac Amaru was an Incan leader.

questions.question: Which Portuguese navigator discovered Ascension Island and Saint Helena in the early 16th century?
questions.explanation_correct: Nova discovered the islands in 1501–1502 during his return voyage from India.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cunha discovered Tristan da Cunha, Cabral explored Brazil, and Albuquerque established bases.

questions.question: Which Portuguese sailor discovered the lonely Tristan da Cunha archipelago in 1506?
questions.explanation_correct: Cunha could not land due to rough seas, but charted the islands that form the most remote inhabited place today.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Nova discovered St. Helena, Cabral Brazil, and Cao explored the mouth of the Congo River.

questions.question: Which Portuguese traveler first explored the mouth of the Congo River in 1482?
questions.explanation_correct: Diogo Cao established first contact with the Kingdom of Kongo and set up stone pillars (padrao) along the coast.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Dias rounded Africa later, Gama reached India, and Zarco discovered Madeira.

questions.question: Which Portuguese sailor discovered the island of Madeira in 1419, launching Henry the Navigator's exploration era?
questions.explanation_correct: Zarco and Tristao Vaz Teixeira landed on Madeira after their ship was blown off course by a storm.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Cao explored the Congo, Eanes rounded Cape Bojador, and Perestrelo colonized Porto Santo.

questions.question: Which Portuguese sailor first rounded the dreaded Cape Bojador on the West African coast in 1434?
questions.explanation_correct: Eanes' success dispelled medieval fears of boiling equatorial waters, opening the way south.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Zarco discovered Madeira, Cao explored the Congo, and Noli discovered Cape Verde.

questions.question: Which Venetian sailor in Portuguese service discovered some of the Cape Verde islands in 1456?
questions.explanation_correct: Cadamosto explored the Senegal and Gambia rivers, describing the islands in reports for Prince Henry.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Noli was his companion and governor, Polo lived in the 13th century, and Cabot explored America.
